title: Interceptor harness for RBAC v2: just-in-time policy eval, explainable decisions, and unified audit sink
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an interceptor/harness that provides a single, lightweight authorization middleware used by API gateway, runtime inference surface, and console routes. Core responsibilities: 1) perform JIT policy evaluation using the new RBAC v2 policy engine; 2) attach structured, explainable allow/deny metadata to responses for admin debugging and audit; 3) emit guaranteed-at-least-once audit events to the unified audit sink; 4) support admin-scoped actions (impersonation, escalate, scope override) guarded by guardrails; 5) integrate with SSO/SAML session attributes for attribute-based rules. This ticket implements the middleware shim, decision cache hooks, and the audit connector used by all call sites.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API/runtime/console requests are passed through the interceptor and receive short-circuited denies when policy blocks; 2) Decision objects include explainability fields: matched rule id, principal attributes, policy version, reason summary; 3) Decisions written to audit stream with schema v1.2 and to the local dev/test sink; 4) JIT eval respects per-request time budget (default 5ms) and falls back to precomputed allow lists when timed out; 5) Feature flag to enable middleware per service and canary rollout to 20% of traffic; 6) End-to-end tests covering allow/deny, impersonation guardrail, SSO attribute propagation, and audit emission pass in CI.
design_notes:
- Policy engine will expose a binary decision API (EvaluatePolicy(principal, resource, action, context)) returning decision + explainability map.
- We adopt a hybrid cache: prefix-indexed allow sets for common low-cardinality checks + per-request LRU decision cache for high-cardinality lookups.
- Explainability will be a compact list of matched rule ids and a human-readable summary for console admins. No secrets or PII are stored in explanation payloads; sensitive attributes are hashed per KMS policy.
- Audit events are canonicalized JSON lines forwarded to kafka://redwood-audit and backed up to s3/archive with retention policy. Events include decision_id, trace_id, actor_id, resource, action, policy_version, outcome, latency_ms, and reason_keys.
- Middleware surface: Go gRPC/HTTP interceptor with pluggable policy client so console (Node), runtime (Go), and API gateway (Envoy filter) can wire in the same evaluation semantics.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Aggressive caching reduces policy eval cost but risks stale allow lists during rapid rollouts; mitigation: include policy_version in cache key and invalidate on policy publish.
- Explainability increases audit payload size; mitigation: use key lists and store verbose blobs in the audit store only when an admin requests a full trace.
- JIT eval budget may cause false-deny if timed out; mitigation: implement graceful fallback to conservative allow lists and a metrics counter to track timeouts.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement minimal EvaluatePolicy gRPC endpoint in policy-engine service (iface + proto). 2) Build interceptor library in go/internal/authz with decision cache and policy client adapter. 3) Add explainability shaping and event serializer. 4) Wire audit producer (kafka) and local dev sink. 5) Add feature flag config and runtime canary via rollout controller. 6) Integrate SSO attribute extractor in the session middleware and propagate to evaluator. 7) Add CI integration tests and chaos test for cache invalidation. 8) Release behind feature flag and run 2-week canary, then promote.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for policy client adapter and cache eviction.
- Integration tests: simulate SAML session with attributes and assert policy outcomes and audit payload.
- Load test: validate middleware p95 added latency < 8ms at 10k rps with warm cache.
- Security test: verify no PII in explanation payloads and that hashing with KMS key rotates correctly.
- Canary run: 20% traffic for 2 weeks with rollback criteria (timeout rate >1% or denied-by-timeout >0.5%).
rollout_steps: 1) Deploy policy-engine endpoint and interceptor library to staging. 2) Enable middleware feature flag in staging. 3) Smoke test console, API, and runtime paths. 4) Canary 20% in production for console only for 48 hours. 5) Expand canary to API/runtime for 7 days. 6) Full enable after 14 days if metrics stable. 7) Post-mortem if rollback triggered.
